cards: Ivan III was Grand Prince of Moscow in the late fifteenth century, often called Ivan the Great.
Mehmed II was an Ottoman sultan who conquered Constantinople in 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire.
Christopher Columbus was a Genoese navigator whose voyage of 1492, funded by the Castilian crown, reached the Caribbean.
Prince Henry the Navigator was a fifteenth-century Portuguese prince, a son of King João I, who took part in the capture of Ceuta in 1415.
Ferdinand II of Aragon was king of Aragon whose marriage to Isabella of Castile united the two crowns.
Philip the Good was Duke of Burgundy from 1419 to 1467.
Afonso de Albuquerque was a Portuguese commander and governor of Portuguese India who held office from 1509 to 1515.
Charles the Bold was Duke of Burgundy from 1467, ruling the Burgundian lands of France and the Low Countries.
Francisco de Almeida was a Portuguese nobleman and the first viceroy of Portuguese India.
Pachacuti, born Cusi Yupanqui, was the ninth Sapa Inca, ruling from about 1438 to 1471.
Władysław II Jagiełło, known in Lithuanian as Jogaila, was Grand Duke of Lithuania who became King of Poland after marrying Queen Jadwiga under the Union of Krewo of 1385.
The Yongle Emperor was the third emperor of the Ming Empire, reigning from 1402 to 1424 after seizing the throne from his nephew.
Túpac Inca Yupanqui was the son of Pachacuti and Sapa Inca from about 1471 to 1493.
Uzun Hasan was the ruler of the Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen confederation, who died in 1478.
Maximilian I was a Habsburg ruler, King of the Romans from 1486 and Holy Roman Emperor from 1508 until his death.
Zheng He was a Chinese admiral and court eunuch who led seven great maritime expeditions for the Ming Empire between 1405 and 1433.
Frederick II, called Irontooth, was Elector of Brandenburg from 1440 to 1470, son of Frederick I.
Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba, known as the Great Captain, was a Castilian general who fought in the conquest of Granada and then commanded Spanish armies in Italy.
Leonardo Bruni (c. 1370–1444) was an Italian humanist and historian who served as chancellor of Florence in 1410–1411 and again from 1427 until his death.
Louis XI was King of France from 1461 to 1483.
Mary of Burgundy was the only child of Charles the Bold and heiress of the Burgundian State.
Matthias Corvinus, son of John Hunyadi, was elected king of Hungary in 1458.
Pope Julius II, born Giuliano della Rovere, was pope from 1503 to 1513 and known as the 'warrior pope'.
Charles VIII was King of France from 1483, governed in his minority by his sister Anne of France and her husband Peter of Bourbon.
Jami was a fifteenth-century Persian poet and Sufi scholar, active in Herat.
Johannes Gutenberg was a fifteenth-century German craftsman who developed printing with movable metal type in Europe.
Pope Sixtus IV reigned from 1471 to 1484.
Aldus Manutius was an Italian humanist and printer who founded the Aldine Press in Venice in the 1490s.
Cesare Borgia was the son of Pope Alexander VI.
Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian painter, engineer and scientist of the High Renaissance, born at Vinci near Florence.
Muhammad Shaybani was the leader of the Uzbeks who conquered Transoxiana and Khorasan in the early sixteenth century.
Abu'l-Khayr Khan was a Shibanid descendant of Genghis Khan who ruled the nomadic Uzbeks of the steppe east of the Ural River from 1428 until his death.
Frederick I, Elector of Brandenburg, was a Hohenzollern burgrave of Nuremberg who supported Sigismund's election as king.
Frederick III was a Habsburg duke of Inner Austria who became King of the Romans in 1440 and the last emperor crowned in Rome, in 1452.
Isabella I of Castile was Queen of Castile who, with her husband Ferdinand of Aragon, united the Spanish crowns.
Kabir was an Indian mystic poet and saint of Varanasi whose verses influenced the Bhakti movement; some historians place his life in 1398–1448, others in 1440–1518.
Lorenzo Valla was an Italian humanist, rhetorician and scholar.
Ausiàs March was a Valencian knight and poet, the leading lyric poet of medieval Catalan literature.
Axayacatl was the sixth tlatoani of Tenochtitlan, ruling in the later fifteenth century.
Casimir IV Jagiellon was Grand Duke of Lithuania from 1440 and King of Poland from 1447.
